results.title: U.S. consumer sentiment falls in August 2026, ending recovery

results.content:
NEW YORK, Aug. 25, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index® decreased by 0.8 points to 89.4 (1985=100) in August, down from 90.2 in July. The Present Situation Index—based on consumers' assessment of current business and labor market conditions—rose by 6.8 points to 121.2, following three months of consecutive decline. results.content: In the second quarter of 2026, US consumers faced uneven hiring, rising inflation, and ongoing geopolitical tensions. Against that backdrop, a smaller share of consumers reported feeling more optimistic about the economy, while a greater share said they felt pessimistic. Consumers also reported intentions to pull back spending across most discretionary categories.
